claim: Standard Schema is a family of TypeScript specs (StandardSchemaV1) authored by the Zod, Valibot and ArkType maintainers to let tools accept any compliant schema without adapters.
quote: The Standard Schema project is a set of interfaces that standardize the provision and consumption of shared functionality in the TypeScript ecosystem. Its goal is to allow tools to accept a single input that includes all the types and capabilities they need — no library-specific adapters, no extra dependencies.

claim: The StandardSchemaV1 Issue interface carries only `message` and `path` — no error code, no params — so a consumer of Standard Schema cannot re-translate errors itself; v1.1 adds StandardTypedV1 and StandardJSONSchemaV1.
quote: export interface Issue { /** The error message of the issue. */ readonly message: string; /** The path of the issue, if any. */ readonly path?: ReadonlyArray<PropertyKey | PathSegment> | undefined; }

claim: @standard-schema/spec reached 1.0.0 on 2025-01-27 and 1.1.0 on 2025-12-15; it is the version in use in July 2026.
quote: latest: 1.1.0

claim: Zod 4 is 14.71x faster at string parsing, 7.43x at arrays, 6.5x at objects vs Zod 3; core bundle drops from 12.47kb to 5.36kb; tsc instantiation blowups on .extend()/.omit() chains drop from ~4000ms to ~400ms; adds a unified `error` param, a locales API, z.stringbool() and z.toJSONSchema().
quote: 14.71x faster than zod3 ... instantiations ... 4000ms to 400ms

claim: Zod 4 unifies error customisation behind a single `error` param with precedence schema-level > per-parse > global (z.config) > locale, and ships 40+ locales in zod/locales.
quote: import { en } from "zod/locales"; z.config(en());

claim: z.coerce.* schemas have an input type of `unknown` by default; z.stringbool() parses "true"/"1"/"yes"; .transform() changes the output type while input stays a string, which is why react-hook-form derives form values from z.input<>.
quote: The input type of these coerced schemas is unknown by default.

claim: Zod Mini is a tree-shakable, functional variant: 2.12kb vs 5.91kb for a simple schema, 4.0kb vs 13.1kb for a complex one, at the cost of a more verbose .check()-based API; Zod's own docs advise against it on the backend.
quote: Zod Mini (2.12kb) vs Zod (5.91kb) ... Zod Mini (4.0kb) vs Zod (13.1kb)

claim: For a login-form schema Valibot bundles to 1.37 kB vs Zod's 17.7 kB (esbuild) and Zod Mini's 6.88 kB; Valibot's runtime speed is 'midfield' — roughly on par with Zod v4, far behind TypeBox/Typia.
quote: Valibot: 1.37 kB ... Zod: 17.7 kB (esbuild) ... in terms of runtime performance, Valibot is in the midfield

claim: Valibot composes validation and transformation with v.pipe(), which must start with a schema and takes up to 19 further schemas/actions; transformation actions change both value and type.
quote: a list of schemas and actions that synchronously passes through the input data

claim: Valibot ships @valibot/i18n as modular submodules plus setGlobalMessage/setSchemaMessage/setSpecificMessage with specific > schema > global precedence, selected via setGlobalConfig({ lang }).
quote: setSpecificMessage(v.minLength, (issue) => `Invalid length: ...`, 'custom'); setGlobalConfig({ lang: 'custom' });

claim: ArkType co-authored Standard Schema and integrates with react-hook-form (@hookform/resolvers/arktype), tRPC 11+, Hono, oRPC and drizzle-arktype.
quote: ArkType is proud to support and co-author the new Standard Schema API with Valibot and Zod

claim: ArkType handles string-to-typed-data with morphs: type("string.numeric.parse"), .pipe(), and filter (validates input pre-morph) vs narrow (validates output post-morph).
quote: type("string.numeric.parse |> number % 2")

claim: ArkType customises errors via an arktype/config global entrypoint, .configure() per type (shallow only), scope- and keyword-level config; it has no locales package and its docs call i18n 'still a topic we're working on'.
quote: this is still a topic we're working on investigating and documenting

claim: @hookform/resolvers v5 ships a generic standardSchemaResolver alongside 20 library-specific resolvers; the comparison table shows Standard Schema, Zod, Valibot and Yup all infer values from the schema and support criteriaMode firstError|all, while ArkType's dedicated resolver is firstError-only and Joi cannot infer values at all.
quote: | Arktype |  ✅ | `firstError` | ... | joi |  ❌ | `firstError \| all` | ... | Standard Schema  | ✅  | `firstError \| all` |

claim: TanStack Form accepts any Standard Schema library (Zod, Valibot, ArkType, Effect/Schema) natively with no adapter, but its validators do not hand back transformed values.
quote: validation will not provide you with transformed values

claim: next-safe-action validates Server Actions against any Standard Schema v1 library with no adapter, calling schema['~standard'].validate(input) directly, so different actions in one project can use different schema libraries.
quote: next-safe-action supports any validation library that implements the Standard Schema specification

claim: Next.js 16's official forms guide still hard-codes Zod for Server Action validation with schema.safeParse(...) + error.flatten().fieldErrors surfaced through useActionState — and the sample still uses the removed Zod v3 `invalid_type_error` option.
quote: For server-side validation, you can use a library like zod to validate the form fields.

claim: Conform's parseWithZod strips empty values and coerces FormData strings to the schema's types by introspecting the schema and injecting preprocessing via coerceFormValue — the same schema then runs in onValidate on the client and in the Server Action.
quote: By default, parseWithZod will strip empty value and coerce form value to the correct type by introspecting the schema and inject extra preprocessing steps using the coerceFormValue helper internally.

claim: A practitioner migrating two forms to Valibot in 2026 saved ~18 KB gzipped and ~140 ms LCP, but kept Zod server-side because drizzle-valibot lagged drizzle-zod — landing on 'client-bundled schemas go to Valibot, server-side schemas stay on Zod'.
quote: client-bundled schemas go to Valibot. Server-side schemas, especially anything shared with the database, stay on Zod.

claim: Third-party 2026 benchmark: 5-field object validation ~8M ops/s ArkType, ~6M TypeBox (compiled), ~4M Valibot, ~2M Zod v4, ~300K Zod v3; ArkType ~20 KB gzipped and its compile time can become the bottleneck on very large schemas, mitigated by .scope().
quote: ArkType | ~8M ... TypeBox (compiled) | ~6M ... Valibot | ~4M ... Zod v4 | ~2M ... Zod v3 | ~300K

claim: Yup 1.7 is Standard Schema compatible, so it plugs into any Standard-Schema-consuming form library.
quote: Yup is compatible with Standard Schema.

claim: Joi 18 implements the Standard Schema `~standard` property including the JSON Schema converter, and depends on @standard-schema/spec ^1.1.0.
quote: Provides compatibility with the Standard Schema specification. It contains a jsonSchema object with the following methods: input([options]) - returns the JSON Schema for the input value (before conversion).

claim: ArkType markets itself as 'TypeScript's 1:1 validator, optimized from editor to runtime' and claims ~20x faster runtime validation than Zod.
quote: ArkType: TypeScript's 1:1 validator, optimized from editor to runtime

claim: Zod's latest release is 4.4.3 (July 2026); npm reports ~224M weekly downloads — more than react itself (~153M/week).
Valibot's latest release is 1.4.2 (July 2026), ~14.3M weekly npm downloads.
quote: valibot@1.4.2

claim: ArkType's latest release is 2.2.3 (July 2026), ~1.2M weekly npm downloads.
quote: arktype@2.2.3

claim: Yup's latest release is 1.7.1 (July 2026), ~10.1M weekly npm downloads.
Joi's latest release is 18.2.3 (July 2026), ~17.8M weekly npm downloads, and it now depends on @standard-schema/spec.
Valibot ships first-class coercion actions such as toNumber() and toDate() for use inside v.pipe().
quote: toNumber | Valibot

claim: Conform is a FormData-first, progressively-enhanced form library for Remix/Next.js that runs one schema on both client and server.
quote: Conform is a type-safe form validation library utilizing web fundamentals to progressively enhance HTML Forms with full support for server frameworks like Remix and Next.js.

claim: next-safe-action is the dominant typed Server-Action wrapper and is Standard-Schema-native.
quote: Type safe and validated Server Actions in your Next.js project.

claim: @hookform/resolvers v5.4.0 (May 2026) is the current release and infers input and output types from the underlying schema.
quote: @hookform/resolvers@5.4.0

claim: Zod 4 replaces ZodError.flatten()/.format() with the top-level z.flattenError() and z.treeifyError(); flattenError yields { formErrors, fieldErrors } — the shape Server Actions hand back to useActionState.
quote: z.treeifyError() provides a nested shape (replacing .format()), and z.flattenError() provides a shallow form (replacing .flatten()).
